title: Project Design  Engineer (Distribution Solutions)
desc:
At
ABB
, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.
This position reports to:
Engineering Manager
__
Your Role And Responsibilities
Working as a Project Engineer, you will be the support person for various MV primary AIS switchgear engineering projects in MV primary AIS, Electrification, Distribution Solutions, providing technical details, costs and deliverables for sales proposals. In this role, you will make technical recommendations in various phases of customer projects to ensure successful delivery of project deliverables on time, within budget and in line with quality and safety guidelines.
Working location: Dilovası Kocaeli (Hbyrid Model)
Key Responsibilities
Following up the project from beginning to the delivery
Making electrical design using the necessary tools and programs (E-Plan, AutoCAD)
Making protection relay programming
Preparing the documentations for design output,
Following non-conformance reports and taking necessary preventive actions
Writing technical and material standards
Working on standardization projects
Qualifications
Graduated from Electrical Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electrical Teaching, Automation Engineering or relevant departments
Minimum 5 years of experience in design of switchgear projects (Experience in Low Voltage Switchgears or Medium Voltage Switchgears will be plus)
Good command of written and spoken English is must
E-Plan knowledge is preferable
Analytical mindset with strong planning and self-learning skills
Strong ability to follow up and pay attention to the details in the projects
Suitable to work with different projects at the same time
Building a cleaner, smarter future takes all kinds of minds: the curious, the courageous, and the creative. That's why we welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences.
